# Scaleway Review 2026: What the European Cloud Costs After the June Price Rise

Scaleway review 2026: instance, storage and GPU prices after the June increase, the IPv4 and storage costs the list prices leave out, sovereignty claims versus certifications, support costs and account risks.

P The Proof Desk 12 min read

☰ Contents 11

Scaleway built its name on very cheap European cloud servers. In June 2026 it raised prices for the first time in three years, and the cheapest instance went up fourfold.

This review uses Scaleway's current pricing pages, documentation and status history to show what you really pay for instances, storage, bare metal and GPUs. It also checks how far the sovereignty claims go, and what support and account risks come with the platform.

## Verdict: still cheap at the bottom, but no longer a bargain bin

Scaleway is the cloud arm of the French Iliad group. It runs regions in Paris, Amsterdam and Warsaw, with a first Milan zone live and Sweden and Germany announced. It sells everything from a sub-euro virtual machine to an eight-way B300 GPU server, along with object storage, bare metal, serverless and hosted AI models.

On 1 June 2026 Scaleway raised prices for the first time in three years. It blamed rising RAM and storage hardware costs and the global IPv4 shortage. The smallest instance now costs four times what it did, every flexible IPv4 address went up 25%, and GPUs rose by roughly 5-10%. Over the same months Dedibox and Elastic Metal got cheaper, B300 GPUs arrived and Milan opened, so the picture is mixed rather than simply worse.

### Our verdict

Scaleway is a good choice for European teams that want EU-owned infrastructure, hourly billing and a broad catalogue at fair prices. Budget for the IPv4 and storage, which the headline prices leave out, and do not buy it for SecNumCloud, which it still does not hold. Low-touch hobby accounts should know that public reviews report account locks.

- Best for: EU-based startups, AI teams that want per-minute H100 billing in Europe, and anyone who needs data kept out of US jurisdiction.
- Watch out for: IPv4 and block storage billed on top of every instance, low quotas until you verify your identity, paid support for fast responses, and no hard spending cap.
- Prices in this review are in euros excluding VAT, taken from Scaleway's pricing pages on 3 October 2026.

## What changed in the June 2026 price increase

Scaleway announced the rise in an April 2026 blog post titled "A transparent update on Scaleway pricing". It says the company had "proudly held our prices flat" for three years, and that anything not on its list keeps its old price. These are the changes most customers will notice:

- STARDUST1-S: €0.00015 to €0.0006 an hour (4x, roughly €0.11 to €0.44 a month).
- DEV1-S: €0.0088 to €0.00898 an hour; DEV1-M €0.0198 to €0.0202; DEV1-L €0.042 to €0.04284.
- PLAY2-PICO: €0.014 to €0.01428; PRO2-XXS: €0.055 to €0.0561 an hour.
- Flexible IPv4: €0.004 to €0.005 an hour. The same increase applies to Bare Metal, Public Gateway and Load Balancer IPs.
- H100-1-80G: €2.73 to €2.87 an hour; H100-SXM-8-80G: €23.03 to €25.33; L40S-1-48G: €1.40 to €1.47; L4-1-24G: €0.75 to €0.79.
- Block Storage SSD: €0.000118 to €0.00013 per GB per hour; Object Storage Multi-AZ: €0.00002 to €0.000022.
- Load Balancer GP-S: €0.016 to €0.023 an hour; Public Gateway S: €0.0199 to €0.026; DNS zone for external domains: €0.001 to €0.007.
- Serverless Functions: €0.000012 to €0.000017 per GB-second.
- Elastic Metal EM-I220E-NVMe: €199.99 to €229.99 a month; Dedibox Core-10-XS: €119.99 to €134.99.

Most general-purpose instances moved about 2%, which almost nobody will notice. The changes that hurt sit around the instance rather than in it: IPv4, load balancers, gateways and DNS zones went up between 30% and 600%. A small stack with a load balancer and a gateway now costs noticeably more than it did in May, even if its instances barely changed.

## Instance pricing: what you actually pay

Scaleway's instance list prices include egress and IPv6, but the pricing page says plainly that "Storage (local, block) and attached public IPv4 addresses are excluded." These are the current list prices, with the monthly figure worked out as the hourly price times 730 hours:

- STARDUST1-S (1 vCPU, 1 GB, 100 Mbps): €0.0006/h, about €0.44/month. Only in fr-par-1, nl-ams-1 and pl-waw-2.
- DEV1-S (2 vCPU, 2 GB, 200 Mbps): €0.00898/h, about €6.55/month.
- DEV1-M (3 vCPU, 4 GB): €0.0202/h, about €14.74/month.
- DEV1-L (4 vCPU, 8 GB): €0.04284/h, about €31.27/month.
- BASIC2-A2C-4G (2 vCPU, 4 GB): €0.023/h, about €16.79/month.
- PLAY2-PICO (1 vCPU, 2 GB): €0.01428/h, about €10.42/month.
- PRO2-XXS (2 vCPU, 8 GB, 350 Mbps): €0.0561/h, about €40.95/month.
- POP2-2C-8G: €0.0735/h, about €53.65/month, up to POP2-64C-256G at €2.35/h.

### The IPv4 now costs more than the cheapest server

A flexible IPv4 is €0.005 an hour, or about €3.65 a month, which is more than eight times the price of a STARDUST1-S. Scaleway's GitHub Instances FAQ still quotes the old €0.004 rate, so trust the network pricing page instead. Some realistic monthly totals:

- STARDUST1-S + IPv4 + 10 GB block storage: about €0.44 + €3.65 + €0.95 = roughly €5.
- DEV1-S + IPv4 + 20 GB block storage: about €6.55 + €3.65 + €1.90 = roughly €12.10.
- IPv6-only workloads skip the €3.65, which is the easiest saving on the platform if your users and dependencies can reach IPv6.

### Billing rules worth knowing

- CPU instances are billed per hour of uptime, including startup and standby time. Each resource has a 60-minute minimum.
- GPU instances are billed per minute, except RENDER-S, which is billed per hour.
- Public IPs and volumes are billed for the whole time they are allocated, "regardless of whether the Instance is powered off." Powering off does not make a server free. You have to delete the IP and the volumes.
- Savings Plans promise up to 25% off compute if you commit to a monthly spend.

## Storage, egress and networking

Object storage is one of Scaleway's strongest products. Requests and ingress are free, and the first 75 GB of egress each month is included, with €0.01 per GB after that. Per month that works out to:

- Standard Multi-AZ: €0.01606 per GB, about €16 per TB.
- Standard One Zone: €0.00803 per GB, about €8 per TB. It was cut in January 2026 and then nudged up again in June.
- Glacier: €0.00254 per GB, about €2.54 per TB, plus €0.009 per GB to restore.
- Block Storage: €0.00013 per GB per hour at 5K IOPS (about €0.095 per GB a month) and €0.000177 at 15K IOPS.
- Local instance storage: €0.000049 per GB per hour.

Instance egress is already included in the list price, which is unusual among the large clouds and a real advantage for bandwidth-heavy workloads. The managed networking add-ons took the largest relative increases in June, so price a Load Balancer GP-S (now €0.023 an hour) and a Public Gateway into any production design.

One console spans buckets in Paris, Amsterdam and Warsaw.

## Elastic Metal and Dedibox: the parts that got cheaper

If you want a whole physical machine, Scaleway has two product lines, and both got cheaper at the entry level over the past year.

- Elastic Metal EM-A116X-SSD (Xeon E3 1220, 32 GB, 2 x 1.02 TB SSD): €27.99 a month or €0.077 an hour, no setup fee.
- Elastic Metal EM-A610R-NVMe (Ryzen PRO 3600, 32 GB): €39.99 a month or €0.11 an hour.
- Remote access became free on every Elastic Metal server in December 2025.
- Dedibox Start-2-S-SSD (4 GB DDR3, 120 GB SSD, 250 Mbps): €4.99 a month, cut from €7.
